## TL;DR

The full-screen diff view is served by one shared `DiffView.vue` behind four
routes (task diff, conflict diff, repo working diff, commit diff). Its Back
control was a 28px-tall chip (`padding: 5px 10px`, 13px line, 1px border) that
rendered as 76×28 CSS px on a phone — comfortably wide enough, but under the
app's 44×44 touch floor in height. The fix is entirely CSS: on phone widths and
coarse pointers the Back button gets a 44px floor and fills its toolbar row, and
the keyboard-only `esc` hint beside it is hidden on the same breakpoint, so the
taller control actually frees horizontal room for the filename instead of
taking any. Desktop is untouched (still 75.7×28 with the hint visible). I added
an explicit `:focus-visible` ring using the theme's `--ring` token, plus two
regression tests: a source-level rule check and a table-driven mounting test
that exercises Back on all four routes. Measured in headless Chromium at
390×844 and 320×844 in light and dark themes: 79.66×44 on every route, esc hint
hidden, focus ring `2px solid var(--ring)` with a 2px offset.

## Work and rationale

The control's width was never the problem: "Back" plus the arrow icon, 6px gap
and 20px horizontal padding already produced ~76px. Only the height failed —
28px against a 44px convention. That shaped the fix: rather than redesigning
the control or making it icon-only, I raised its vertical size to the app's
existing mobile floor and kept the label. An icon-only square would have saved
horizontal space but cost clarity for a page whose only escape hatch is this
button; keeping "Back" reads better and the acceptance criteria only demand the
44px box.

I modelled the treatment on `.drawer-mobile-back` in `style.css`, the app's
existing phone Back control (task-detail drawer): it uses `display: inline-flex`,
`min-width: 44px`, `min-height: 44px`, `padding: 0 9px` and a `:focus-visible`
outline, applied at `max-width: 719.98px`. Matching it keeps two Back controls
that appear in the same product flow visually and behaviourally consistent
instead of inventing a third pattern.

Two details are deliberate:

- **Breakpoint:** `@media (max-width: 719.98px), (pointer: coarse)`. Width alone
  would miss tablets in landscape, where a thumb is still the input; the
  `pointer: coarse` arm covers those, including hybrids whose primary pointer is
  touch. The repo already keys keyboard-affordance hiding off
  `hover`/`pointer: coarse` (#1139), so this is the established vocabulary.
- **Hiding the `esc` hint on the same breakpoint:** the hint is a
  keyboard-only affordance and meaningless on a touch phone. Because it sat to
  the right of the button with a 6px gap, removing it returns ~30px to the
  filename — more than the vertical growth costs anything. The topbar stays at
  its 48px height, and the 44px button sits inside it with 2px top/bottom, so
  the diff viewport loses nothing vertically either.

I did not shrink the toolbar padding or restructure the topbar. The filename
already has `flex: 1; min-width: 0` with ellipsis, so it absorbs any squeeze,
and the delta/status chips sit outside it. Scope stayed on the Back control —
the file-tab arrows are a separate control that the task did not flag.

The focus ring was added because the previous control relied on the browser
default. The repo's convention for page-level controls is a 2px outline in
`var(--ring)` with a 2px offset, and `--ring` is defined for every UI theme pair
(`:root`/light), so it reads correctly in all theme packs rather than only the
default. The `esc` hint remains in the DOM (hidden only at the mobile
breakpoint) because a landscape tablet with a hardware keyboard can still use
Escape.

Tests were chosen to cover both the CSS intent and the routing surface. The
shared view is mounted four ways, and the task explicitly asks for all four to
be verified; a table-driven `it.each` over the four routes asserts the Back
control renders and calls `router.back()`. The source-level assertion in
`mobile-touch-affordances.test.ts` keeps the 44px rule and the hidden hint from
silently regressing, in the same spirit as the existing #1139 assertions on
`style.css`. That file now reads `DiffView.vue` as well as the global stylesheet
because this component's rules are scoped to the SFC.

## Approaches tried

- **Pseudo-element hit area:** considered keeping the visual 28px chip and
  expanding the tap target with an absolutely positioned `::before`. Rejected:
  the measured bounding box stays 28px, which fails the acceptance criterion as
  written and defeats the point of a documented touch floor.
- **Icon-only 44×44 square on phones:** saves ~35px of toolbar width but
  removes the only visible label on a page that is otherwise a wall of code.
  Rejected for clarity; the filename has enough room now that the `esc` hint
  is gone.
- **Bumping the whole topbar to 56px:** would give the button breathing room
  and a larger drag area, but costs 8px of diff viewport on a 844px-tall phone.
  Rejected — the 44px control already fills the existing 48px row and looks
  intentional.
- **`@media (max-width: 719.98px)` only:** simpler, but misses touch tablets
  in landscape, which #1139 explicitly accounted for in the shell. Kept the
  coarse-pointer arm.

## Challenges and blockers

The only surprise was verification, not code. My first headless measurement
pass read `outline: solid 3px` with the theme's `--txt-dim` colour and no
offset, and an inline `outline: 7px solid red` appeared not to apply at all.
That looked like a cascade bug. It was a timing artefact: the view's CSS is a
lazy-loaded chunk (`DiffView-*.css`), and my script measured after the DOM
selector existed but before that chunk was applied — so Chromium's default
focus ring was the only one in play. Waiting for the chunk made the computed
style the intended `2px solid rgb(57,224,255)` with a 2px offset. Worth
remembering for any future UI measurement: wait for the lazy CSS, not just the
selector, and never diagnose a cascade problem from a single early read.

I also had to confirm the working tree was not accidentally edited through the
main checkout: all edits and builds ran under the task worktree, and `git
status` shows only the three intended files.

One follow-up bit me after the first handoff: the declared shots pointed at
`/tasks/1151/diff`, but the managed preview board had no such task, so its API
returned 404 and the page sat on "Loading diff…". Task-scoped data is not
dependable on a preview board; the shots now use the repo-scoped commit route,
which renders the same `DiffView` from `git show`.

## Key learnings

- The app's shared 44px mobile touch floor is not applied globally; each page
  keeps its own media query. Copying `.drawer-mobile-back`'s shape is the
  cheapest way to stay consistent.
- Removing a touch-irrelevant keyboard hint is a way to *pay for* a larger
  control: the visual weight grows vertically while the toolbar actually gets
  less cramped horizontally.
- Scoped SFC styles need their own regression assertions; the existing
  `mobile-touch-affordances` suite only read global CSS, so it was worth
  extending rather than adding another one-off test file.
- Verifying a route-shared component means mounting every route, not just the
  primary one — the route table is the contract, and `it.each` documents it.
